A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable text, figures, and appendices. The original appendices match v2 Appendices A.2–A.5 after insertion of the response to criticisms.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on mathematical benchmarks and four puzzles, including accuracy, pass@k, reasoning-token usage, and failure analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds greedy-decoding experiments, Checker Jumping algorithm-guidance results, and qualitative reasoning examples.

M1.justification: The underlying framework remains evaluation of existing models through move-sequence extraction and deterministic puzzle simulation. The new decoding and algorithm-guidance experiments are controls within this framework.

E1.justification: The three mathematical benchmarks and four puzzle environments remain. v2 narrows large-instance coverage, explicitly excluding Hanoi N>12 and River Crossing N>=6 from the revised sweeps; Checker Jumping and Blocks World plots also cover smaller maximum sizes.

E2.justification: The main model comparisons retain their participants. The first-failure analysis expands from Claude and DeepSeek comparisons in v1 Figure 11 to include o3-mini medium/high configurations in v2 Figure 13.

E3.justification: v2 adds temperature-zero decoding controls and an algorithm-guided Checker Jumping condition. Reported Checker Jumping and Blocks World prompts also drop the minimum-sequence instruction. These are limited extensions and revisions within the retained simulator-based evaluation design and token budgets.

E4.justification: Algorithm guidance, previously tested only on Hanoi, is extended to Checker Jumping in Figure 8. v2 also adds a four-puzzle greedy-decoding ablation, o3-mini failure analyses, and annotated Claude examples of constraint-verification failures and overthinking. These substantially expand tests of explanations for model failure.

E5.justification: Both versions state 25 samples per model, puzzle instance, and complexity level. They retain distribution and individual-sample visualizations without introducing new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Several retained accuracy, pass@k, and failure curves are revised; for example, the R1/V3 Hanoi gap around N=5 is much smaller in v2 Figure 5 than in v1 Figure 4. New results include Hanoi accuracy of 18.2% with sampling versus zero with greedy decoding at N=8. Large-instance results are removed and additional control results reported; matched-protocol performance gains are not established.

T1.justification: The compositional-depth definition and puzzle complexity formulas remain unchanged. The expanded discussion of branching factors, finite problem sizes, and training exposure adds interpretation without new formal derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: Several introduction and contribution statements qualify collapse from zero to near-zero, although the abstract retains complete-collapse wording. Inconsistent execution is now explicitly framed across problems and scales. The central three-regime and reasoning-effort claims remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1 substantially expands arguments about context limits, sampling, River Crossing restrictions, algorithm familiarity, and tool use. Section 4.4 and Appendix A.4 also emphasize within-puzzle complexity comparisons and training-distribution explanations. These materially expand causal interpretations and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v2 newly describes response-format filtering and supplies the Checker Jumping algorithm prompt, while removing the explicit Hanoi initialization/calling instructions. Candidate-format validation and solution deduplication were already documented in v1. The PDFs do not establish whether response-level filtering was newly implemented.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bender et al. on stochastic parrots, Zubić et al. on sequence-modeling complexity, and Ruoss et al.'s LMAct, while removing the Marcus blog reference. Related-work positioning expands modestly toward theoretical complexity and decision-making evaluations.

P1.justification: The main section sequence remains intact, with localized rewriting, terminology changes, and expanded discussion in Section 4.4. A response-to-criticisms section is inserted before the existing appendices, which are renumbered.

P2.justification: Accuracy and pass@k figures exchange order, numerous plots receive revised axes and ranges, and the former combined Figure 8 becomes expanded algorithm and failure displays. New comparison plots and annotated reasoning-trace boxes substantially change presentation. Existing density and intermediate-solution plots are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: The new greedy control and restricted problem ranges address important alternative explanations. However, the added Checker Jumping pseudocode in Appendix A.3 ignores successful returns from TryMove and falls through to null, weakening its execution-only interpretation. Revised retained accuracy curves are also not clearly reconciled with the newly described filtering. These benefits and validity concerns prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
